card.name: Word starts in older quoted prose
card.fires_on: The letter h (or H) beginning a word such as hoot, honor, hogsheads, Halloween, and some other short words in older, literary or quoted prose.

modes.label: Lone h starting a word
modes.description: The letter h stands alone as the start of a word split into pieces, inside a quote or verse.
modes.example: I let out a<< h>>oot and it bounced for 20

modes.label: Common words in archaic prose
modes.description: Ordinary words like shall, are, has, most, or committed in formal 19th-century or legal-style passages.
modes.example: The odds<< are>>, that though he has never thought of

card.writes: It slightly favors word pieces like hell and Hell and disfavors crude or sexual words, so the effect is weak and mixed.
card.plain: It fires on the first letter h of words in old-fashioned quoted writing, plus a few scattered formal words.
